name: Perfume Genius
label: Matador
lede: Mike Hadreas left a Seattle-area high school in his senior year and put piano songs on Myspace. Matador put out the record, he played Letterman, and a dance score with a saxophonist and a string arranger became his sixth album.

eras.title: A Seattle bedroom and a Myspace page
eras.text: Hadreas grew up in the Seattle suburbs, left for New York, came back, and started recording piano songs at home. He put them online under a name taken from a movie.

years.h: Born in Des Moines, raised in the Seattle suburbs
years.p: Mike Hadreas moves to the Seattle suburbs at six or seven. He studies painting and takes piano lessons.
years.xp: Wikipedia gives his birth as September 25, 1981. His mother worked as a special education teacher and later as an assistant principal.

years.h: A New York doorman goes home to Seattle and starts recording
years.p: Hadreas works the door at an East Village club, then returns to Seattle in 2005 and records at home.
years.xp:
Wikipedia reports he dropped out of high school in his senior year after threats the administration ignored, and was attacked by several young men two years later. He then moved to Williamsburg, Brooklyn.

The Fader adds that he partied hard in New York and came home to a 20-day rehab. The songs that became Learning started after that, recorded at his mother's house.

years.h: The Myspace page goes up with a name from a murder film
years.p: Perfume Genius is the protagonist of Tom Tykwer's 2006 film Perfume: The Story of a Murderer.

eras.title: Matador, a pianist, and a flagged video
eras.text: Learning comes out on Matador, Hadreas meets the pianist who becomes his partner, and the second record's video gets flagged by YouTube.

years.h: A mutual friend introduces him to his future pianist and partner
years.p: Alan Wyffels is a classically trained pianist. He becomes Hadreas's touring pianist, then his partner.
years.xp: The Fader says the friend hoped Wyffels could help Hadreas get sober, and that Wyffels took him to AA meetings. Wikipedia says they began dating soon after. Wyffels co-wrote Glory and plays on the later records.

years.cap: Hadreas at Matador at 21, Las Vegas, October 2010
years.h: Matador picks up Learning after the Myspace page spreads
years.p: Many of the songs were recorded at home. Matador handles the US, Turnstile Europe, and Pitchfork gives it 8.2.
years.xp:
Wikipedia credits the Myspace page for the attention that led to the release.

His first live show was at the Vera Project in Seattle, opening for A Sunny Day in Glasgow. Wyffels played piano on the tour that followed.

years.cap: Hadreas at the Prospect Park Bandshell, Brooklyn, 2012
years.h: YouTube flags a hug as unsuitable for family audiences
years.p: The promo video for Put Your Back N 2 It has Hadreas embracing adult performer Arpad Miklos.
years.xp: The record drew a second round of praise. Wikipedia reports the YouTube flag.

years.h: A guest vocal on Cate Le Bon's Mug Museum
years.p: Hadreas sings on "I Think I Knew", the first of many collaborations outside his own records.

eras.title: Too Bright, and a late-night debut
eras.text: Hadreas brings in a Portishead co-producer for a bigger sound, then takes it to Letterman. Prada and the Grateful Dead catalog follow.

years.cap: Perfume Genius at The Independent, San Francisco, October 2014
years.h: Portishead's Adrian Utley co-produces Too Bright
years.p: Utley and Ali Chant produce. Pitchfork gives it 8.5 and Best New Music; Metacritic lists it at 87.
years.xp:
Adrian Utley of [[Portishead|8f6bd1e4-fbe1-4f50-aa9b-94c450ec0f11]] and Ali Chant co-produced. The album reached No. 83 on the US Billboard 200 and No. 77 in the UK, per Wikipedia.

"Queen" and "Grid" went on to turn up in TV series including Mr. Robot and The Great.

years.h: David Letterman's audience gets "Queen"
years.p: His late-night TV debut, on The Late Show with David Letterman.

years.h: Sharon Van Etten joins him on a Grateful Dead song
years.p: "To Lay Me Down" goes on Day of the Dead, a Red Hot Organization benefit tribute released May 20, 2016.

years.h: Prada puts his Elvis cover in a perfume ad
years.p: "Can't Help Falling in Love" runs in campaigns for La Femme and L'Homme.

eras.title: Blake Mills and the big pop record
eras.text: With producer Blake Mills, Hadreas makes the two albums Pitchfork scores 8.8 and 9.0, and starts curating as well as writing.

years.h: "Slip Away" gets a video from Björk's collaborator
years.p: Andrew Thomas Huang, who has worked with [[Björk|87c5dedd-371d-4a53-9f7f-80522fb7f3cb]], directs it. Pitchfork tags the song Best New Track.

years.cap: Hadreas at the Pop Conference, Seattle, April 2017
years.h: Blake Mills produces No Shape in Los Angeles
years.p: Recorded October to December 2016. Pitchfork gives it 8.8 and Best New Music.
years.xp:
Shawn Everett mixed it. Pitchfork called it "his most realized album yet, a tender and transcendental protest record." It was nominated at the 60th Grammys for Best Engineered Album, Non-Classical, and Pitchfork later ranked it No. 70 on its 200 best albums of the 2010s, according to Wikipedia.

The Fader put him on its March/April cover that year; in that story he spoke about his sobriety and about living with Crohn's disease since childhood.

years.h: Hadreas curates Le Guess Who? in Utrecht
years.p: His picks include Aldous Harding, Mount Eerie, Weyes Blood and Le Mystère des Voix Bulgares.

years.h: "Otherside" plays in the trailer for The Goldfinch
years.p: The film adapts Donna Tartt's novel.

years.src: Wikipedia: Set My Heart on Fire Immediately
years.h: Sound City, Pino Palladino, and his highest Metacritic score
years.p: Recorded at Sound City in Van Nuys with Blake Mills. Pitchfork gives it 9.0 and ranks it No. 5 of 2020; Metacritic has it at 91.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists bassist Pino Palladino, drummer Matt Chamberlain, violinist Rob Moose and Phoebe Bridgers on harmony vocals. Hadreas named Townes Van Zandt, Enya and the Cocteau Twins among his influences.

"Describe" came out February 25 and "On the Floor" March 16, ahead of the album.

eras.title: Ugly Season, a dance piece that kept going
eras.text: The pandemic pushes Hadreas toward a stage project. He scores a dance with Kate Wallich, then decides the music should stand on its own.

years.h: Kate Wallich and Hadreas build The Sun Still Burns Here
years.p: Hadreas writes the score for the Seattle choreographer's piece, with Alan Wyffels improvising on it.
years.xp:
Hadreas told Document Journal the project started because he and Wallich decided to make a dance performance together. He added that he'd never made anything where someone else was involved from the very beginning.

Mills produced, and the music was always meant to exist on its own, too.

years.cap: Hadreas at All Points East, London, August 2022
q: It can be an album, a dance piece, a short film, all of it.
years.h: Ugly Season leaves the stage for Matador
years.p: Ten tracks, 52 minutes. Pitchfork gives it 8.6 and ranks it No. 26 of 2022; Metacritic's average across 18 critics is 79.
years.xp:
Wikipedia credits Blake Mills with production and lists saxophonist Sam Gendel, string arranger Rob Moose and drummer Matt Chamberlain. Paste gave it 8.4 and put it at No. 23 on its year-end list. It reached No. 39 on the UK Independent Albums chart.

Hadreas told Billboard the record could be an album, a dance piece or a short film; artist Jacolby Satterwhite directed that film, Pygmalion's Ugly Season.

years.h: Back on the road after the pandemic
years.p: Hadreas tells Billboard from Sydney that he enjoys live performing "way more than I ever have".
years.xp: Billboard spoke to him from Sydney, after the New Zealand dates.

eras.title: Glory, and a wedding
eras.text: Hadreas covers a standard for a TV series, then returns with another Blake Mills record that Wyffels co-wrote.

years.h: Jack Antonoff produces a standard for Apple TV
years.p: Hadreas covers "What a Diff'rence a Day Makes" for the series The New Look.

years.h: Blake Mills produces Glory, and Wyffels co-writes
years.p: Announced January 15 with "It's a Mirror", which Pitchfork tags Best New Track. Aldous Harding guests.
years.xp: Wikipedia also lists Jim Keltner, Meg Duffy and Gregory Uhlmann. Hadreas and Wyffels married in 2025, per the same article.
